description:
Found by the reviewing session (s542) while probing s540d`s const-fold; PRE-EXISTING (main 24988e35).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
  BEGIN { no strict "refs"; *{"main::Y"} = sub () { 7 }; }
  print Y, " ", Y + 1, "\n";
  perl: `7 8` + newline.   PCL: `7 7`, no newline, NOTHING on stderr.

WHAT HAPPENS: Y has no record at parse time, so `Y + 1, "\n"` is read as a list-operator call Y(+1, "\n"); perl knows the `()` prototype from the BEGIN block and reads `Y() + 1`.  docs/static-parse-limits-review-s512.md line 56 classes "run-time glob assignment" as "no parse effect in perl either" -- true at RUN time, NOT inside BEGIN.  This is the same family as `BEGIN { use_ok(...) }` (#4881): a BEGIN block changes what the parse knows.

TWO QUESTIONS, cheapest first:
 1. THE DETECTOR (#2610, default `announce`): a call of a name that was unknown at parse time and that at RUN time turns out to be a sub with a `()` prototype, given arguments, is exactly its shape -- why is it silent here?  (Cheap discriminating measurement: PCL_DETECT=die ./runpcl on the reproducer; then read whether the detector hears a call whose callee was installed by glob assignment rather than by `sub`.)
 2. Whether the parse should read a LITERAL `*{"PKG::NAME"} = sub (PROTO) {...}` / `*NAME = sub (PROTO) {...}` statement directly in a BEGIN body as a prototype declaration (a mechanism keyed on the shape, like #4881).  A census over the board + perl`s t/ decides whether it is worth it; not started.

Not a regression and not s540d`s; filed so the silent wrong has a number.

MEASURED (s542, question 1`s first half): `PCL_DETECT=die ./runpcl` on the reproducer prints `7 7` and exits 0 -- the detector does not hear this call at all, so it is not an announce-level question.
subject: A `()`-prototype sub installed by a BEGIN-time glob assignment (`BEGIN { *{"main::Y"} = sub () { 7 } }`) is unknown to the parse: `print Y, " ", Y + 1, "\n"` prints `7 7` with no newline (perl `7 8`), and the #2610 detector does NOT announce it
triage_reason: a `()` sub installed by a BEGIN-time glob assignment is unknown to the parse
